profile.campus: QTS Phoenix campus, 85 acres, planned as five data centres
profile.reading:
This building sits at 1200 North 40th Street in Phoenix, Arizona, one of five buildings QTS operates on what the company calls its 40th Street campus, an 80 acre site in the Phoenix metro's east-central industrial corridor. QTS's own current site lists the campus's five addresses as 1200, 1250, 1400, 1450, and 1500 North 40th Street, and this row's coordinates place it at the first of those, 1200 North 40th Street, so this record identifies it as the campus's earliest or first-numbered building (QTS's public materials label the campus DC1 through DC5 but do not publish a clean map of which street address corresponds to which DC number). QTS's own site states the whole campus provides more than 210 MW of critical capacity, a figure describing the five-building campus combined rather than this single building, and QTS does not publish a separate power or square footage figure for this building alone on that page. An earlier trade press report about the campus groundbreaking cited a larger planned figure near 280 MW for eventual full buildout, which this record treats as a forward-looking construction plan rather than the capacity QTS currently states as built, since the two figures are not confirmed to describe the same measurement.

QTS describes the 40th Street campus as built on a standardized design intended for rapid, large scale deployments, with a redundant fiber conduit system running express fiber to each building and providing for connections between future buildings as the campus fills in. That design approach, purpose built shells added incrementally as demand grows, is typical of how large colocation operators phase in wholesale campuses rather than building every building to full specification on day one.

This building and its four siblings are a separate site from QTS Phoenix 1, the carrier hotel suite QTS leases inside 120 East Van Buren Street in downtown Phoenix, roughly four and a half miles to the southwest. That downtown building, tracked separately in this registry, is a Digital Realty owned multi-tenant carrier hotel where QTS holds space alongside other operators including LightEdge and AIS, acquired through QTS's 2015 purchase of Carpathia Hosting. The 40th Street campus, by contrast, is land QTS controls directly and has built out as its own wholesale campus, a different kind of asset serving a different purpose, and the two sites should not be treated as one facility despite both carrying a QTS Phoenix label in different contexts.

QTS itself, headquartered in Overland Park, Kansas, was taken private in August 2021 when three Blackstone vehicles, Blackstone Infrastructure Partners, Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust, and Blackstone Property Partners, jointly completed an acquisition of QTS Realty Trust valued at roughly 10 billion dollars including debt, closing August 31, 2021, according to Blackstone's own announcement. At that time QTS described itself as operating more than 7 million square feet of owned mega scale data center space across North America and Europe, serving hyperscale technology companies, enterprises, and government customers through what it calls a software defined technology platform, and Chad Williams served as chief executive at the time the deal closed. QTS is a wholesale and colocation landlord in the same business category as CyrusOne and Digital Realty, leasing built capacity to tenants rather than running its own end user cloud service. Since the Blackstone deal, QTS has continued expanding in the Phoenix area beyond this 40th Street campus, including a separate roughly 375 acre parcel acquired in Glendale, Arizona in mid 2022 for further development, underscoring how much larger the company's regional footprint has become than any single campus, this one included.
profile.capacity_note: The 42 MW figure QTS gives for this building is capacity, and the 280 MW is the planned figure for the whole 85-acre campus once five buildings are complete. Neither is an IT load figure and neither should be read as one.

reading.body:
QTS operates this building as one of five on an 80-acre campus at 1200 North 40th Street in Phoenix's industrial corridor east of the city center. QTS's own site states the five-building campus provides more than 210 MW of critical capacity combined, but does not publish a separate power figure for this building alone. The campus is designed as a phased wholesale deployment on standardized shells, with shared fiber infrastructure running between buildings as they are added incrementally rather than built all at once. A separate earlier trade report cited a planned 280 MW for eventual full buildout of the site, which may describe a forward construction scenario rather than current built capacity.

Assuming 8 kW per rack as a conservative estimate for colocation IT density, the 210 MW campus capacity suggests roughly 26,000 racks across five buildings, or around 5,200 racks per building on average if evenly distributed. That figure is directional only and does not account for uneven phasing across buildings, reservable capacity sitting idle, or the difference between nameplate power and actual draw. The building's own specifications are not published separately by QTS, limiting precision about what this single facility can actually host.

This campus ranks fifth among the four facilities in Arizona with published megawatt figures, behind larger published sites. Arizona has 57 mapped data center locations across the state but only four with published capacity on operator spec pages, totaling 512 MW. This building contributes to QTS's regional portfolio but sits in a state where most facilities report no public capacity figures and transparency about grid demand remains sparse.
